work.title: Die Patrioten. Ein Singgedicht auf den Geburthstag Sr. königl. Hoheit des Kronprinzens von Dännemark

history.p: For Crown Prince Christian’s birthday in 1760, Scheibe composed the present cantata to a text by his acquaintance, the royal Chaplain Johann Andreas Cramer. It was first performed in the hall of The Musical Society on 29 January. In the beginning of February the cantata was repeated in the royal chambers with the prince present, and according to the newspaper Kiøbenhavns Adresse-Contoirs Efterretninger the performance was followed by great applause. At the event Scheibe was given a golden box and his son, Christian Friedrich who was a military officer, received a pecuniary gift. In 1764, when Scheibe was very much occupied with studying the recitative and its function in music, he employed the cantata as an example analysing various aspects of the work. He published his study in the first part of ‘Abhandlung über das Recitativ’ which appeared in Bibliothek der schönen Wissenschaften, 1764 (SchW C1:003). This is one of the few cantatas to which both music and printed libretto have survived.

annot.p: 'Den forhen i Raadhuusstrædet af det musicalske Sælskab paa Hans Kongelig Høyheds Cronprintsens Fødses Fest den 29 Januarii opførte Concert, blev i Mandags opført paa Slottet, i Hans Kongelig Høyheds Cronprintsens høye Overværelse, og blev anhort med stort Bifald.'

physDesc.watermark: emblem, consisting of a coat-of-arms with a single diagonal band and the fleur-de-lis and the countermark 'IV' or 'VI', is partly visible. The same watermark is also seen in SchW B2:301 and B2:313 suggesting that all three works were most likely produced around the same time. Paper of a dense and rather coarse quality meaning that it is difficult to draw staves on the paper.
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format, consisting of 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 1 nested bifolios; title page (fol. 1r), list of instruments and vocal parts (fol. 1v), music (fols. 2r–63r; numbered 5–125 in ink (Scheibe)), blank page with staves (fol. 63r); in all 63 folios. Hand-ruled paper, between 18 and 21 staves (7 mm; single rastrum used) in brown ink and music in black ink; bottom and top staves on numerous pages have not been used. A clean ink autograph fair copy with only few changes; same source type as SchW B2:301 (D-B, Scheibe 1b and D-B, Scheibe 4).

In original grey limp binding (same as D-B, Scheibe 1a) with raised bands and yellow label ‘Die Patrioten v. Scheibe. | Partitur.’ pasted on spine, presumably in Poelchau’s hand, above ‘10.’ added in ink (perhaps contemporary with Scheibe; pasted on end paste-down is the ex libris ‘Ex | bibliotheca | Poelchavian.’). A modern label has been pasted on the front cover.
